chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib reported to me, saying: Abul Qasim Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Katanji narrated to us, saying: Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I heard al-Ridha Ali ibn Musa, peace be upon them both, say: Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, said to Kumayl ibn Ziyad among what he said:
O Kumayl, your brother is your religion, so be cautious about your religion however you wish.
And all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his family and grant them abundant peace.

key_terms.أخوك: Your brother — refers to a fellow believer, emphasizing that religious brotherhood entails mutual responsibility
key_terms.دينك: Your religion — meaning one's religious welfare and spiritual standing
key_terms.فاحتط: Be cautious/careful — from ihtiyat (precaution), a key concept in Islamic jurisprudence and ethics

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say to Kumayl ibn Ziyad about brotherhood and religious responsibility?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) transmits Imam Ali's advice to his companion Kumayl ibn Ziyad: "Your brother is your religion" -- meaning that the welfare and conduct of your fellow believer directly affects your own religious standing. Kumayl was a devoted companion of Imam Ali known for his deep spiritual relationship with the Imam. This teaching underscores that brotherhood in Islam is not merely social but a sacred religious duty demanding vigilant care.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 9. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib reported to me from Abul Qasim Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Katanji, who reported from Abu Hashim Dawood ibn al-Qasim al-Ja’fari, may Allah bless him with mercy, who said: I heard al-Ridha ‘Ali ibn Musa saying: Once Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, told Kumail ibn Ziyad during his discourse:
"Your brother is your religion (his welfare is your religious responsibility) so be cautious of your religion in what you desire (for him)."
And all praise for Allah, the Lord of the Universe. And may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his progeny.
